authorization: etymologise remaining Indo-Aryan surveys. do not rebuild. work autonomously and do what you can, you have 8 hours, i will review once your time is done.

proposals.evidence: Shackle’s printed muccu entry (p. 243, directly inspected) gives abundant/plenty, big/broad and very, and explicitly prints CDIAL 10178 mucca as its etymology. This supplies the semantic bridge missing from Turner’s shorter lump/heap and Punjabi piece entries. The Awankari/Gujari muc/mūc adjectives are qualified regional members of that family; the comparison does not establish the extent of local historical diffusion.
